accepted.evidence: Turner 12278 śatá '100' explicitly cites European Romani šel. The source prints Zargari śel 'one hundred' in its numeral table (p. 137 §3.5.1) and explains the -i- connector before following numerals (p. 138 §3.5.1.1). This is the simple hundred stem. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

The source prints duy-śel 'two hundred' (p. 138 §3.5.1) and explicitly states that numerals are compounded (§3.5.1.1). Its two source components are attested duy 'two' (already linked to CDIAL 6648) and śel 'hundred' (newly linked to CDIAL 12278). The component edge records this composition, not a separate whole-word Sanskrit ancestor. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

The source explicitly prints śel-i-pānj 'one hundred and five' (p. 138 §3.5.1.1) as its example of -i- before the following numeral. Its two source lexical components are śel 'hundred' (newly linked to CDIAL 12278) and pānj 'five' (already linked to CDIAL 7655); -i- remains the source connector. This records components, not a single ancient compound etymon. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

held.reason: The printed hundred–thousand composition is clear (p. 138), but the source's sila 'thousand' is not established as Indo-Aryan and may be Greek. Hold a full component analysis pending the immediate origin of sila.

The printed '196' form contains the known śel and śov elements but also mixed tens with unresolved contact histories. Do not assign a whole-word historical origin based on the two secure pieces alone.
